title: Shaquille O'Neal
description: American former basketball player and sports analyst (born 1972)
wiki_lead:
Shaquille Rashaun O'Neal (born March 6, 1972), often referred to by his nickname "Shaq", is an American former professional basketball player who is a sports analyst. A 7-foot-1-inch (2.16 m) center, O'Neal played for six different teams over his 19-year career in the National Basketball Association (NBA). He is a four-time NBA champion, three-time NBA Finals MVP, and the 2000 NBA MVP. He is widely regarded as one of the most dominant centers in NBA history and one of the greatest basketball players of all time. 
After playing college basketball for the LSU Tigers, O'Neal was selected by the Orlando Magic with the first overall pick in the 1992 NBA draft. He was named NBA Rookie of the Year in 1992–93 and led his team to the 1995 NBA Finals. After four years with the Magic, O'Neal signed as a free agent with the Los Angeles Lakers. He and the Lakers won the NBA championship in 2000, 2001, and 2002. Amid a feud between O'Neal and his teammate Kobe Bryant, O'Neal was traded in 2004 to the Miami Heat, where he won his fourth NBA championship in 2006. During the last several years of his career he spent short stints with the Phoenix Suns, the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Boston Celtics.
O'Neal's accolades include 15 All-Star Game selections, three All-Star Game MVP awards, 14 All-NBA team selections, three NBA All-Defensive Team selections and two scoring titles. He is one of three players to be named NBA MVP, All-Star Game MVP and Finals MVP in the same year. He ranks 9th all-time in points scored, 6th in field goals, 15th in rebounds, and 8th in blocks. He had a 58.2% career field goal percentage and led the league in field goal percentage ten times. He is a member of the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame and the FIBA Hall of Fame, and was named to the NBA 50th Anniversary Team and the NBA 75th Anniversary Team as one of the greatest players in league history.
In addition to his basketball career, O'Neal has released four rap albums, including the platinum-certified Shaq Diesel (1993) and the gold-certified Shaq Fu: Da Return (1994). Under the name Diesel, he produces electronic music and tours as a DJ. He has appeared in numerous films and has starred in reality shows such as Shaq Vs. and Shaq's Big Challenge. O'Neal is the general manager of the Sacramento State Hornets men's basketball team.

Early life
Shaquille Rashaun O'Neal was born on March 6, 1972, in Newark, New Jersey, to Joe Toney and Lucille O'Neal. Toney had played high school basketball and was offered a scholarship to play at Seton Hall. He struggled with drug addiction and was imprisoned for drug possession when O'Neal was an infant. Upon his release, he did not resume a place in O'Neal's life and relinquished his parental rights to O'Neal's stepfather, Phillip Arthur Harrison, a career Army sergeant. grok_lead: Shaquille Rashaun O'Neal, commonly known as Shaq, is an American former professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the most dominant centers in National Basketball Association (NBA) history. Born on March 6, 1972, in Newark, New Jersey, O'Neal stands at 7 feet 1 inch (2.16 m) tall and weighed 325 pounds (147 kg) during his playing career, using his immense size and athleticism to average 23.7 points, 10.9 rebounds, and 2.5 assists over 1,207 games across 19 seasons with six teams: the Orlando Magic, Los Angeles Lakers, Miami Heat, Phoenix Suns, Cleveland Cavaliers, and Boston Celtics. Drafted first overall by the Magic in 1992 after a standout college career at Louisiana State University, where he was named National Player of the Year in 1992, O'Neal earned NBA Rookie of the Year honors in 1993 and quickly established himself as a force, leading the league in scoring average twice and ranking among the all-time leaders in points (11th), field goals made (eighth), and field goal percentage (15th at 58.2%). O'Neal's pinnacle achievements came during his eight seasons with the Lakers from 1996 to 2004, where he formed a dynasty with Kobe Bryant, securing three consecutive NBA championships (2000â2002) and earning three Finals MVP awards in those years, along with the league MVP in 2000. His fourth championship followed in 2006 with the Heat, solidifying his legacy with 15 All-Star selections, three All-Star Game MVPs, 14 All-NBA honors (eight First Team), and three All-Defensive Team nods. Internationally, O'Neal contributed to the U.S. Olympic team's gold medal at the 1996 Atlanta Games. Inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2016, he was also selected to the NBA's 50th and 75th Anniversary Teams, recognizing his transformative impact on the game through sheer physical dominance and scoring prowess around the basket. Beyond basketball, O'Neal has built a multifaceted career in entertainment, business, and philanthropy. He has appeared in films and television, released platinum-selling rap albums like Shaq Diesel (1993), and served as a studio analyst on TNT's Inside the NBA since 2008, earning widespread acclaim for his charismatic commentary. In business, O'Neal is a prolific entrepreneur with investments in franchises like Papa John's (where he was a board member until 2020), ownership stakes in the Sacramento Kings (2013â2022) and Kings Guard Gaming in the NBA 2K League, and recent ventures including a role as President of Reebok Basketball (announced 2024), partnerships with JCPenney in beauty products (2025), and founding partner in Jacmel Infrastructure (2025). As a philanthropist, he has been the national spokesperson for the Boys & Girls Clubs of America for over 15 years and supported various youth and education initiatives. In 2025, O'Neal took on the role of general manager for the Sacramento State men's basketball program, further extending his influence in the sport.
